scenes.text: Imagine working tirelessly for years of your life on a multi-million dollar spacecraft, only to watch the entire thing explode in a massive ball of fire because of one single keypress.
In 1962, NASA proudly launched the Mariner 1 probe destined for Venus, but just minutes after liftoff, the rocket veered dangerously off course, forcing mission control to blow it up.

When investigators dug into the computer code, they shockingly discovered that a programmer had simply missed a single superscript bar, which was essentially a tiny hyphen, inside the complex guidance formula.

That one missing dash turned a perfect flight into absolute chaos, costing eighty million dollars in today's money, making it the most expensive typo in human history. Would you have spotted this mistake? Comment below and follow!
